name: Total orders
question: How many orders are there? Return one column named total_orders.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_orders FROM orders

name: Completed orders
question: How many orders have completed? Return one column named completed_orders.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS completed_orders FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed'

name: Cancelled orders
question: How many orders are cancelled? Return one column named cancelled_orders.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS cancelled_orders FROM orders WHERE status = 'cancelled'

name: Total customers
question: How many customers are in the database? Return one column named total_customers.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_customers FROM customers

name: Total products
question: How many products are listed? Return one column named total_products.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_products FROM products

name: Orders in 2026
question: Count orders placed in 2026. Return one column named orders_2026.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS orders_2026 FROM orders WHERE order_date >= '2026-01-01' AND order_date < '2027-01-01'

name: Completed orders in 2026
question: Count completed orders placed in 2026. Return one column named completed_orders_2026.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS completed_orders_2026 FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND order_date >= '2026-01-01' AND order_date < '2027-01-01'

name: Cancelled orders in 2025
question: Count cancelled orders placed during 2025. Return one column named cancelled_2025.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS cancelled_2025 FROM orders WHERE status = 'cancelled' AND order_date >= '2025-01-01' AND order_date < '2026-01-01'

name: Orders in Delhi
question: Count orders placed by customers from Delhi. Return one column named delhi_orders.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS delhi_orders FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.city = 'Delhi'

name: Processing or shipped orders
question: Count orders whose status is either processing or shipped. Return one column named active_orders.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS active_orders FROM orders WHERE status IN ('processing', 'shipped')

name: Orders by status
question: Count orders for every status. Return status and order_count, highest count first, breaking ties alphabetically by status.
reference_sql: SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders GROUP BY status ORDER BY order_count DESC, status ASC

name: Revenue by order status
question: Calculate total line-item revenue for each order status. Revenue is quantity multiplied by unit_price. Return status and revenue, highest revenue first.
reference_sql: SELECT o.status, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY o.status ORDER BY revenue DESC, o.status ASC

name: Average completed order value
question: Calculate the average total value per completed order. First total the line items within each order, then average those order totals. Return one column named average_order_value.
reference_sql: WITH order_totals AS (SELECT o.order_id, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS order_value FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY o.order_id) SELECT AVG(order_value) AS average_order_value FROM order_totals

name: Monthly completed revenue
question: Calculate completed-order revenue for each month. Return month in YYYY-MM format and revenue, newest month first.
reference_sql: SELECT SUBSTR(o.order_date, 1, 7) AS month, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY SUBSTR(o.order_date, 1, 7) ORDER BY month DESC

name: Quantity sold by category
question: Calculate the total quantity sold for each product category across all orders. Return category and quantity_sold, highest quantity first.
reference_sql: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS quantity_sold FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY quantity_sold DESC, p.category ASC

name: Revenue by customer city
question: Calculate revenue from completed orders for each customer city. Return city and revenue, highest revenue first.
reference_sql: SELECT c.city, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS revenue FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.city ORDER BY revenue DESC, c.city ASC

name: Product revenue
question: Calculate total sales revenue for every product across all order statuses. Return product_id, product_name and revenue, highest revenue first.
reference_sql: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name ORDER BY revenue DESC, p.product_id ASC

name: Customer order counts
question: Show every customer who has placed at least one order. Return customer_id, name and order_count, highest count first and customer_id ascending for ties.
reference_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.name ORDER BY order_count DESC, c.customer_id ASC

name: Order item totals
question: For each order, calculate its total line-item value. Return order_id and order_value, highest value first, limited to 10 orders.
reference_sql: SELECT order_id, SUM(quantity * unit_price) AS order_value FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id ORDER BY order_value DESC, order_id ASC LIMIT 10

name: Customer latest order date
question: Show each customer who has placed an order and their most recent order date. Return customer_id, name and latest_order_date, newest date first.
reference_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.name, MAX(o.order_date) AS latest_order_date FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.name ORDER BY latest_order_date DESC, c.customer_id ASC

name: Top five products by revenue
question: Show the top 5 products by total sales revenue across all order statuses. Return product_name and total_sales_revenue, highest first.
reference_sql: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales_revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name ORDER BY total_sales_revenue DESC, p.product_name ASC LIMIT 5

name: Top ten customers by completed spending
question: Find the top 10 customers by revenue from completed orders. Return customer_id, name and total_spending, highest first, breaking ties by customer_id ascending.
reference_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_spending FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.name ORDER BY total_spending DESC, c.customer_id ASC LIMIT 10

name: Top five customers by order count
question: Find the top 5 customers by number of orders. Return customer_id, name and order_count, highest count first, breaking ties by customer_id ascending.
reference_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.name ORDER BY order_count DESC, c.customer_id ASC LIMIT 5

name: Top categories by revenue
question: Rank product categories by total sales revenue across all orders. Return category and revenue, highest first.
reference_sql: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY revenue DESC, p.category ASC

name: Top three cities by completed revenue
question: Find the top 3 customer cities by revenue from completed orders. Return city and revenue, highest first.
reference_sql: SELECT c.city, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS revenue FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.city ORDER BY revenue DESC, c.city ASC LIMIT 3

name: Cancellation rate
question: Calculate the cancellation rate as a percentage of all orders. Return total_orders, cancelled_orders and cancellation_rate_pct, rounded to two decimal places.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_orders, SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'cancelled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS cancelled_orders, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'cancelled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 2) AS cancellation_rate_pct FROM orders

name: Top two customers per city with ties
question: For each city, find the top two customers by completed-order revenue. Return city, customer_id, name, revenue and rank_in_city. Use RANK so ties at rank 2 are included. Sort by city, rank_in_city and customer_id.
reference_sql: WITH customer_revenue AS (SELECT c.city, c.customer_id, c.name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS revenue FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.city, c.customer_id, c.name), ranked AS (SELECT city, customer_id, name, revenue, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY city ORDER BY revenue DESC) AS rank_in_city FROM customer_revenue) SELECT city, customer_id, name, revenue, rank_in_city FROM ranked WHERE rank_in_city <= 2 ORDER BY city, rank_in_city, customer_id

name: Products never ordered
question: Find products that have never appeared in order_items. Return product_id and product_name, ordered by product_id ascending.
reference_sql: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name FROM products p WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_items oi WHERE oi.product_id = p.product_id) ORDER BY p.product_id

name: Monthly revenue comparison
question: For completed orders in September and October 2026, return month in YYYY-MM format and revenue, newest month first.
reference_sql: SELECT SUBSTR(o.order_date, 1, 7) AS month, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND SUBSTR(o.order_date, 1, 7) IN ('2026-09', '2026-10') GROUP BY SUBSTR(o.order_date, 1, 7) ORDER BY month DESC

name: Order status percentage
question: Calculate the percentage of all orders represented by each status. Return status and percentage_of_orders rounded to two decimal places, highest percentage first.
reference_sql: SELECT status, ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders), 2) AS percentage_of_orders FROM orders GROUP BY status ORDER BY percentage_of_orders DESC, status ASC
